summary: Restrict to the near points and apply Cauchy–Schwarz.

steps.lean:
nth_grw 1 [pivotModulus, ← lintegral_floorMeasure_congr rfl eqOn_indicator,
    ← setLIntegral_eq_of_support_subset, sq_lintegral_le, hK g, restrict_le_self]
steps.claim: pivotModulus = ∫_{σ : σg near at l+1} |upperPairing(F, l+1, k, σg, σy)| dθ^F_l (the integrand vanishes elsewhere, step 2); by h the integrand is at most √(u(σg)v(σ)), and Cauchy–Schwarz gives (∫_{near} √(u(σg)v(σ)))² ≤ (∫_{near} u(σg) dθ^F_l)·(∫ v dθ^F_l) ≤ K·∫ v dθ^F_l (hK).

steps.lean:
repeat first | fun_prop | simp [indicator, subset_def]; grind [isNear_of_upperPairing_ne_zero,
    zero_le]
steps.claim: Side goals: measurability, and the support: a nonzero upper pairing at (σg, σy) forces σg to be near at l + 1 (isNear_of_upperPairing_ne_zero).
